subject: ventures/medicaid-lookback-penalty-calculator
professional: an elder-law attorney (or Medicaid planner) who prepares nursing-home applications: first checks that the 60-month window, the divisor arithmetic and the penalty start date follow 42 USC 1396p(c), then that no transfer is silently treated as exempt when it is not

evidence.correctness: Imported calc.mjs and recomputed against the statute (42 USC 1396p(c)(1)(B)(i) 60 months; (E)(i) penalty = uncompensated value / average monthly private-pay cost; (E)(iii) start when otherwise eligible and institutionalised) with a separate hand calculation. (1) gifts 45,000 + 30,000 = 75,000, divisor 10,500: 7.142857 months, 7 months + floor(0.142857*30)=4 days; tool gave 7 and 4, penalty end 2027-05-05 (2026-10-01 + 7 months + 4 days); care gap (11,500-2,800)*(7+4/30)=62,060, tool 62,060. (2) 100,000 at divisor 12,000: 8.3333 months = 8 months 10 days, end 2027-06-11; tool identical. (3) window edge: application 2026-10-01, gifts on 2021-10-01 and 2021-09-30 of 21,000 each: only the first counts (60 months inclusive), tool total 21,000. Leap-day application 2024-02-29 gives start 2019-02-28 and counts only the 02-28 gift, consistent with calendar-month subtraction. Departures: penalty start is the typed application date, not the later of that and the first of the month of transfer, which only matters when the application precedes the transfer month (not possible, such gifts error). Exemption detection is wrong in several cases, see defects. Arithmetic is right, classification is not.
evidence.completeness: Claimed in README/VENTURE.yaml/page and checked by running calc: in-window test, penalty months and days, care bill after income, effect of returned money, application-date sweep table (0 to 60 months), age-out date per gift, summary text and CSV download, validation errors named per line. All present and exercised by compute() and the tests. Not checked in a browser (no browser run here), the HTML wiring was only read and grepped. VENTURE.yaml stage is 'prototype' and states no attorney has verified it.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/medicaid-lookback-penalty-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 25 tests, 25 pass, 0 fail, 0.33 s. Seeded mutations, each reverted with git checkout (git status clean): (a) window comparison 'x.date >= start' changed to '>' -> 1 test failed (caught). (b) 'Math.max(0, gross - input.returned)' changed to ignore returned -> 1 test failed (caught). (c) partial-day factor '(months - whole) * 30' changed to '* 31' -> 25 of 25 still passed (NOT caught): the only partial-day test has a 0.048-month fraction where 30 and 31 both floor to 1. Also no test of the exemption word list on false positives, no test with a real state divisor, no test of leap-day or month-end window starts.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (169 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs and index.html metadata in full. Pure functions with no DOM or network, UTC date maths that clamps month ends, input validation that names the field, floating-point tolerance (1e-9) on floor. Defects: EXEMPT_WORDS is a bare keyword regex over a free-text note (calc.mjs:9) so any note with 'disabled', 'trust', 'sibling', 'spouse' or 'blind' removes the gift from the total, including 'not disabled' and 'spouse's cousin'; partial-month days use a fixed 30-day month; the lookback input has an empty default. Otherwise clean and small.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'Everything runs in your browser, nothing is sent' -> page.test.mjs asserts no fetch/XHR/beacon in index.html or calc.mjs, and passes; disclaimer 'not legal, tax ... advice' and 'No warranty' present (tested); 'Not decided' list on the page and README. Page FAQ lists the federal exemptions correctly (spouse, blind/disabled child, trust for disabled, caregiver child home, sibling with equity interest) and says the state decides. Unbacked or stale: llms.txt links to duncan-haywood.github.io, not marisstella.app (CLAUDE.md says Pages only redirects); sitemap.xml has a relative './index.html' loc, which is not a valid absolute sitemap URL; the page and tool treat a bare word 'sibling' or 'trust' as exempt although the FAQ says only an equity-interest sibling and only disabled-person trusts are exempt; README test command uses a glob the repo notes warn about.
evidence.fitness: Walked an adult child's job: enter a parent's five gifts with a state divisor, get the count inside the window, penalty months and days, the end date, care cost during it, and when each gift ages out. Worked end to end through compute(). Hurdles an attorney or family hits quickly: no state divisor table (the user must find it; stated design choice for liability), no handling of the community spouse, the home, annuities or promissory notes, no multiple-applicant or married-couple split, and the free-text exempt word can silently understate the penalty with no warning on the mis-keyed row beyond a generic 'some transfers are marked exempt'.
evidence.domain: Compared against 42 USC 1396p(c) (DRA 2005): 60-month look-back, divisor = average monthly private-pay cost, penalty begins when otherwise eligible, cumulative transfers, return of assets can cure, partial-month treatment left to the state. The model follows that. An elder-law attorney would flag: exemptions are a keyword guess rather than a category the user picks; no note that a sibling or child exemption for the home requires specific conditions; no warning about transfers into trusts (look-back for trusts can differ) beyond a note; no state-specific penalty start nuances (some begin on the first of the month); partial return treatment is shown as a flat reduction. The disclosed limits are honest.

defects.what: Exemption is decided by a keyword regex on the free-text note, so notes such as 'daughter, not disabled', 'niece, trust fund', 'sibling' or 'spouse's cousin' remove the gift from the total (probe: each of these returned a countable total of 0 for a 21,000 gift in window), understating the penalty a family would plan around
Partial-day conversion '(months - whole) * 30' is not pinned by any test: changing 30 to 31 leaves all 25 tests green
llms.txt points to the retired github.io host instead of marisstella.app, and sitemap.xml uses a relative loc './index.html' that crawlers will not accept
No tests with a real state divisor or month-end and leap-day window starts; no usage of the community spouse or home exemption categories as explicit choices

verdict: A small, honest prototype whose arithmetic is right: three hand recomputations from 42 USC 1396p(c) (penalty months and days, end date, care gap, window edge) matched exactly, and 25 of 25 tests pass. It does not meet the bar because verification is only partly effective (one of three seeded mutations, the 30-day month factor, survived) and because the exemption logic is a keyword guess that silently zeroes out gifts whose note merely contains words like 'disabled' or 'trust', which an elder-law attorney would reject first. The page's disclaimers and no-upload claim are backed by tests, but llms.txt and sitemap.xml are stale. Browser behaviour was not exercised here, so the HTML layer is scored from reading only.
